scope: Read-only research and candidate authoring; no operating assets, indexes, generation pointers or runtime changed.

sources.title: American Academy of Dermatology: 11 ways to reduce premature skin aging
sources.supports: Facial lines and changes in fullness are visible ageing features; timing varies. This supports possible local depiction, not an exact age estimate.

sources.title: American Academy of Dermatology: What can make my hands look younger?
sources.supports: Hand ageing can be expressed by fine folded skin and reduced fullness. These are optional visible cues, not proof of age, disease or a life history.

sources.title: World Health Organization: Ageing and health
sources.supports: Older adults vary considerably; chronological age does not prescribe one appearance, capacity or dependency. Exact age remains requester-provided context.

corpus_inspection.method: Inspected global unfiltered documents and all checked canonical bodies using installed BodyReader.record plus photo_canonical_source.native. Compared full decoded installed meanings against current V3 content, conditions and effects; did not compare raw V3/V4 serialization. Broad wrinkle scan included cloth and expression confusions; source meanings, not tag membership, determined relevance.
corpus_inspection.working_source_result: Four useful adjacent CIDs match the decoded installed meanings; none has an age effect. No age-dimensional effects were found in the checked installed corpus.

confusion_boundaries: Requester-specified seventies is a declaration. Visible facial or hand features cannot verify that range or replace it with an estimated age.
A visible skin fold from bending, squinting or contact alone is not explicit older age presentation.
Each age-appearance assignment stays with its named actual region. Face appearance does not become hand appearance or whole-person chronological age.
Adult/human intrinsic conditions remain prerequisites. A smoother-looking adult region neither creates a child nor relaxes adulthood.
Age appearance gives no health, dependency, personality, ancestry, occupational wear, family relation, treatment history or identity conclusion.
Skin color, gray hair, age spots, visible veins and frailty are not mandatory older-person components. Aged fabric or a synthetic surface is not human skin ageing.
An age-presentation option that also authors microtexture must declare both age and appearance effects. Existing property locks and requester identity still apply.
The two contrast options are alternatives. They cannot be unioned into contradictory values on the same selected region.
recommendations: Integrate only after explicit owner and native-effect review, retaining both age and appearance footprints and all adult/human guards.
Keep chronological age in requester declarations and local older/younger-looking presentation in separate region-specific properties.
Use the existing elderly commuter, grandmother and celebration records only for their actual subject/context meanings, not as proxies for local age depiction.
Run the parent unchanged-query before/after retrieval and inspect actual top candidates. This source-gap finding does not establish a retrieval improvement.
Bind generic face/hand targets to the request-existing owner and actual selected region; do not create a new person, a hand count or missing body inventory during integration.
